submission.justification: Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 92.8% at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate. This significantly exceeds the 80% minimum requirement and outperforms Algorithm-L1 (85.3% at 30 GeV) and Algorithm-L3 (which fails to meet the 80% requirement at any tested threshold between 20-60 GeV). The 30 GeV threshold was found to be optimal through systematic scanning - efficiencies were lower at both higher and lower thresholds. Algorithm-L2 uses iterative topological clustering with learned calibration, which provides superior signal/background discrimination. According to candidate_specs.md, all three algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs), and there are no documented latency concerns. The 2025 simulation summary confirms Algorithm-L2's strong performance. This recommendation maximizes signal efficiency while meeting all hard constraints.

requirements.requirement: Signal efficiency at allocated rate must be at least 80%
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV achieves 92.8% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, significantly exceeding the 80% minimum requirement.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: According to candidate_specs.md, all candidate algorithms fit within the FPGA resource budget (LUTs, DSPs). No latency concerns were raised in any project documents including meeting notes and simulation summaries. All three algorithms were presented as viable candidates, implying they meet basic feasibility criteria including latency constraints.
The recommended threshold of 30 GeV falls within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Achieve highest possible signal efficiency at allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Through systematic threshold scanning (20-45 GeV) across all three algorithms, Algorithm-L2 at 30 GeV was found to provide the highest signal efficiency of 92.8%. This exceeds Algorithm-L1's best performance (85.3% at 30 GeV) and Algorithm-L3's performance at all tested thresholds.
